title: Inferring driver intent increased aligned steering assistance in a simulator study
summary: In an urban driving simulator, 8 of 11 participants with paired observations received more steering assistance aligned with their intent under the intent-conditioned policy. Collisions occurred in 4 of 147 intent-conditioned trials, 10 of 130 trials with assistance lacking intent inference, and 2 of 121 unassisted trials.
ai_technology: Dream2Assist; recurrent state-space world model; reinforcement learning

source_review.scope: v1 urban simulator human study, §6.4 objective results and preliminary on-vehicle scope

evidence.tested: Participants experienced within-subject simulator trials under intent-conditioned, non-intent, and unassisted conditions in randomized order. Physical driving was only a preliminary deployment.
evidence.unknown: Trial counts are repeated within people and collisions were concentrated among a few participants. The measurements do not establish an on-road safety benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A trained recurrent world model infers driver intent and conditions the assistance policy. The same architectural comparator omits the intent predictor.
